title: Lesson 1.2 Knowledge Check
description: Five questions on computational thinking in loop-based production. Unlimited attempts; your best score counts.

questions.text: Breaking a beat into kick, snare, hi-hat, bass, and chord layers is an example of which computational thinking move?
questions.feedback: Decomposition means breaking the whole into parts you can work on separately.

questions.text: In a 4/4 bar shown as sixteen cells, where does the standard backbeat snare fall?
questions.feedback: Beats 2 and 4 of the bar are cells 5 and 13. The kick sits on 1 and 9; hi-hats on every odd cell give straight eighth notes.

questions.text: A well-made 16-bar beat usually contains sixteen completely different bars.
questions.feedback: Most beats repeat a four-bar phrase with deliberate variations. Repetition gives stability; variation gives interest.

questions.text: Which of these are places where AI makes decisions inside a modern digital audio workstation? Select all that apply.
options: Loop recommendation based on key and tempo
The color of the track header
Pattern generation in a chosen style
questions.feedback: Loop recommendation, mastering, and pattern generation all make musical choices for you. Track colors are cosmetic.

questions.text: Your numbered list of variations (fill at bar 4, drop bass at bar 8, new element at bar 9, silence before bar 13) is best described as:
options: An algorithm: an ordered set of steps
questions.feedback: An ordered list of changes applied to the form is algorithm design.
